GTA 6: Watch the First Hour of Gameplay and the First Two Chapters
78 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
I’ve always hated giving spoilers, but GTA 6 is here , and you really need to watch this first hour of gameplay. It’s more of a movie than a game, as Rockstar wanted to make sure you get to know Lucia, Jason, their past, and how they ended up together.
I’ve never seen so many people loving to watch cutscenes, to be honest. Rockstar used the first two chapters in GTA 6 not only to introduce you to the game, but also to help you get to know the people that’ll guide you throughout this fascinating new adventure in the city of Leonida.
In many ways, GTA 6 starts just like a romance film, with Lucia and Jason getting to know each other when they are about to get arrested. Because I don’t want to give more spoilers, let’s just say that the story continues with Lucia being away from Jason, who continues to do things that you obviously shouldn’t do.
GTA 6 is another top-notch mix of ridiculous nudity, depraved life, crime, fantastic music, and everything else that we’ve grown to love for over one decade in Grand Theft Auto V . It’s almost emotional to be able to play GTA 6 after all these years, just to get the old GTA feeling in a completely modern and refreshed appearance.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Everything feels and is new. The cars - because we’re at autoevolution here, so we’re obsessed with cars - look much more realistic, and the control isn’t by any means as arcade-ish as it was in GTA 5. It’s obviously not Gran Turismo, but it’s very clear that developers have spent a reasonable amount of time to get this right.
The dynamic weather system that Rockstar is so proud of makes the game feel more realistic, but at the same time, it also makes driving more challenging, especially at night. The level of glare during night driving when it’s raining makes perfect sense, and anyone wearing glasses will tell you that Rockstar got this right.
The car crashes aren’t necessarily as realistic as I expected them to be, but you’ll get a lot of feedback whenever you collide with another vehicle. That’s a good thing because crashes are not supposed to be as common as they were in GTA 5. I mean, yes, they are there, and you can always hit another vehicle on the road, but you’d better not do this too often because it’s much, much harder to get out of a major fender-bender with the police on your tail.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Stealing cars is also more difficult than in GTA V. If you’re like me, you’ll probably rush to the first car you see out there immediately after you finish the first chapters and Brian gives you the first missions. You won’t be able to steal any cars from your neighborhood - you know, you’re supposed to be a good neighbor, after all - and most cars you see parked on the side of the road are locked.
The only option would be to smash the side window, much like the Kia Boys do in real life , but this approach will result in a police report that’ll have a patrol car sent after you in a matter of seconds. The car alarm will fire up, so you’ll better leave the area as fast as possible. Returning to the area after a couple of minutes, even if police are not on your tail anymore, is not a good idea because officers will continue to patrol the neighborhood and look for you.
Drivers show some resistance when you’re trying to take them off their cars and steal them. You’ll have to fight them, though this is quite easy, but if a police officer is nearby, that’ll get you into trouble. Truck drivers are obviously the most likely to engage in a fight, but aside from hitting you once or maybe twice, they won’t be able to stop you from stealing their vehicles.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Driving and listening to music while respecting the law continues to be ridiculously satisfying. I lost count of how many times I did this in GTA 5, and now that GTA 6 is here with improved graphics and mechanics, just driving around and listening to the fantastic tunes on the radio - often laughing because it’s still GTA and the people on the radio drop all kinds of references to real life - is a very relaxing way of playing this game.
I’ll drop a spoiler now. Lucia won’t be around for your first missions, and that’s why Jason shows up more, including when Brian sends him to bring home the checks. She’ll eventually be there, but now’s the time to grab the popcorn and watch the first hour of gameplay, which could very well be a Hollywood movie, considering the story and graphics.
You'd better not skip the cutscenes when you start playing GTA 6. Meanwhile, I'm already working on the full review, so stay tuned for the full details.
